tracks.title: The Firefly Post Office
tracks.creativeDirection: A firefly post office carrying wishes through a summer night

segments.text: [softly] Settle into a position that feels kind enough for today. Imagine a tiny post office opening after sunset, staffed by patient fireflies.
Begin with a message addressed to you. May I be safe... may I be cared for... may I have moments of ease. Let the words glow without demanding that you believe them perfectly.
A firefly lifts the message gently and carries it around the quiet rooms of your body. Perhaps warmth arrives. Perhaps awkwardness does. Both can receive mail here.
Now picture someone easy to wish well. Place their name on another small envelope. May you be safe... may you be cared for... may you have moments of ease.
Watch that light travel across gardens, rooftops, and sleeping streets. You do not need to know how the message lands.
Bring to mind a familiar stranger... someone seen on a bus, in a shop, or through a neighbouring window. Their life contains rooms you have never entered.
May you be safe... may you be cared for... may you have moments of ease. Another firefly rises into the common dark.
[thoughtfully] Include someone difficult only if that feels workable. You can offer a modest wish without approving their actions: may wisdom and kindness become more possible.
Let the post office grow busy now. Thousands of small lights carry wishes toward animals, strangers, friends, and people awake beneath unfamiliar skies.
May we be safe... may we be cared for... may we have moments of ease. Let the sentence be a direction of the heart, not a promise about the world.
Release the words and feel the body breathing. The fireflies can continue their work without your supervision.
[softly] Return to the room. Open your eyes when ready, carrying one small undelivered kindness into the rest of your day.

tracks.title: Paper Boats Under the Moon
tracks.creativeDirection: Paper boats carrying kindness down a moonlit canal

segments.text: [softly] Let the body be supported. Imagine a moonlit canal beside you, smooth enough to carry a small paper boat.
Write a wish for yourself on the first boat: may I be protected from unnecessary harm... may I know friendship... may I rest when rest is needed.
Set the boat on the water. If self-kindness feels difficult, let the canal hold the wish until you are ready to receive it.
Fold another boat for someone you love. Picture their ordinary face, including the details that make them human rather than perfect.
May you be protected from unnecessary harm... may you know friendship... may you rest when rest is needed. Watch their boat join yours.
Now choose a person who usually stays at the edge of your attention. A stranger has a whole weather system of memories too.
Offer the same wishes and let a third boat drift into the silver current. No emotion is required; intention is enough for this moment.
If it feels possible, include someone with whom life is complicated. Keep your boundaries. Simply wish that suffering and confusion do not keep multiplying.
[reassuringly] You may skip anyone who makes the practice unsafe. Loving kindness includes the person sitting here, and that person is allowed to choose distance.
Imagine the canal widening into a river filled with paper lights. May all of us find safety... connection... and enough gentleness for the next step.
Let the river travel beyond imagination. Feel your hands, your breathing, and the quiet place where the boats began.
[softly] Open your eyes when ready. Keep one blank boat nearby for a kindness you have not thought of yet.

tracks.title: Below the Blue Portholes
tracks.creativeDirection: An underwater station gently closing its outer portholes

segments.text: [softly] Close your eyes if comfortable and imagine resting inside a quiet station beneath a blue ocean. Nothing outside needs to vanish.
Hear the furthest sound as though it travels through water to reach you. Receive the vibration, then let it continue past.
Notice nearer sounds... the room... clothing... breathing. Each is a small instrument panel reporting that the world is still there.
Imagine one outer porthole becoming softly frosted. Sight grows less important for a while, without being forced away.
Feel temperature on the skin, then let attention sink beneath it toward pressure, weight, and the slow movement of the belly.
Taste and scent may be faint. Let those channels rest too, like underwater microphones placed on standby.
[thoughtfully] The senses keep working; Pratyahara changes your relationship with their messages. You can hear a knock without opening every door.
Choose one inner sensation: heartbeat, breath, warmth, or the simple feeling of being contained by the body.
If an outer signal brightens, notice it and let it dim naturally. Return to the quiet pressure of the ocean around the station.
Rest in the inner room for several breaths. No perfect silence is necessary. Even the deep sea contains distant songs.
Begin clearing the portholes. Include sound, temperature, light behind the eyelids, and the shape of the whole body.
[softly] Move gently and open your eyes. Rise from the blue station slowly, keeping its quiet room somewhere within reach.

tracks.title: The Library After Closing
tracks.creativeDirection: A vast library closing its sensory reading rooms for the night

segments.text: [softly] Settle as though you have entered a library just after closing. The building remains awake, but no new information is required.
Listen to distant sounds as books being returned somewhere far between the shelves. Let each thump and whisper belong to its own aisle.
Notice nearby sounds, then imagine the listening desk lowering its lamp. Hearing continues without becoming the main assignment.
Behind closed eyes, let the reading room of sight grow dim. Shapes and colours can remain like illustrations in books you do not need to open.
Notice touch at the skin... then deeper contact and weight. Choose the simplest sensation as a bookmark for attention.
Allow taste and scent to become background notes in the catalogue. Nothing is rejected; it is simply filed for later.
Turn inward toward breath, pulse, or warmth. Imagine a private reading room where the only text is the body happening now.
[reassuringly] A loud sound or thought may reopen a door. Gently close it after the message arrives, without blaming the librarian.
Rest between the shelves of inner sensation. There is no need to find a secret book or achieve blankness.
For a little while, let awareness read only one quiet page... inhale... exhale... pressure... warmth.
Now switch on the outer rooms again. Hear the building, feel the air, and notice light waiting beyond the eyelids.
[softly] Open your eyes and leave the library unhurriedly. The quiet page remains available whenever you return.

tracks.title: The Last Train Enters the Depot
tracks.creativeDirection: A night train settling carriage by carriage into a quiet depot

segments.text: [softly] Lie down and adjust anything that needs support. This is deliberate rest, not a substitute for sleep. Imagine the last train of the evening entering a quiet depot.
Feel the left foot and toes as the first carriage becomes still... sole... heel... ankle... calf... knee... thigh.
Let the whole left leg rest on its track. Nothing to lift, brace, or carry.
Move through the right toes... sole... heel... ankle... calf... knee... and thigh. The second line powers down.
Feel both legs together, heavy or light, detailed or vague. The depot accepts every kind of arrival.
Notice pelvis, hips, and lower back. Let the belly move without instructions while the central carriage settles.
Feel lower ribs, chest, shoulder blades, and upper back. With each exhale, another overhead light clicks off.
Travel through the left fingers, palm, wrist, forearm, elbow, upper arm, and shoulder. Let the arm be parked for the night.
Now right fingers, palm, wrist, forearm, elbow, upper arm, and shoulder. Allow both hands to release their imaginary luggage.
Notice throat, jaw, lips, tongue, cheeks, and the tiny muscles beside the nose. Let the face stop announcing where it is going.
Feel eyes, brow, forehead, temples, ears, and scalp. The destination board becomes blank.
Sense the whole head... whole torso... both arms... both legs. The train is complete and motionless enough.
[reassuringly] You may be awake, dreamy, restless, or nearly asleep. Rest does not require a particular platform.
[softly] Deepen the breath. Move fingers and toes, stretch if wanted, and return as the depot begins switching on its morning lights.

tracks.title: The Seaside Hotel Turns Down the Lights
tracks.creativeDirection: A seaside hotel becoming quiet room by room

segments.text: [softly] Lie down comfortably and let the surface receive you. This practice offers deep rest while leaving sleep to do its own important work.
Imagine a seaside hotel after midnight. Begin at the left toes, foot, ankle, calf, knee, and thigh as rooms along the west wing go dark.
Feel the right toes, foot, ankle, calf, knee, and thigh. Curtains close softly along the east wing.
Notice both legs and the pelvis. Let their weight sink like luggage finally placed on the floor.
Move through lower belly, lower back, ribs, chest, and upper back. The lift stops humming; the lobby clock keeps time alone.
Feel left fingers, hand, wrist, forearm, elbow, upper arm, and shoulder. Let every key be returned to the desk.
Now right fingers, hand, wrist, forearm, elbow, upper arm, and shoulder. Both arms can be entirely off duty.
Notice throat and neck... jaw... lips... tongue... cheeks. Let the face become an unoccupied room.
Feel the eyelids, space around the eyes, brow, forehead, temples, ears, back of the head, and scalp.
Hear any distant sound as surf beyond the hotel windows. It can roll in and out without requiring attention.
Sense the whole body at once, from scalp to toes. The building rests beside the ocean and breathing continues like a quiet tide.
[thoughtfully] Nothing has to feel heavy. Nothing has to disappear. Let rest be the absence of another assignment.
Remain here for several breaths while the hotel keeps its patient watch beside the dark water.
[softly] Invite movement back into hands and feet. Open your eyes slowly, as though morning has reached the curtains.

tracks.title: A Forest of Small Transmissions
tracks.creativeDirection: Forest sounds becoming a map of near and distant transmitters

segments.text: [softly] Close your eyes if comfortable and imagine every sound as a small transmitter hidden in a night forest.
Hear the whole forest at once. Let sound arrive before the mind decides what made it.
Choose the most distant signal. Rest attention there as though a tiny lamp is blinking beyond the trees.
Now find a middle-distance sound... something neither far away nor inside your body.
Tune to the nearest sound: breath, fabric, swallowing, or a quiet movement beside you.
Move from far... to middle... to near... allowing attention to travel without rushing.
Notice a sound beginning, changing, and ending. No transmission remains exactly itself.
[thoughtfully] Release the categories and hear one living field. The forest needs no conductor.
Include the body that is listening and the silence that appears between signals.
[softly] Open your eyes. Let the forest become an ordinary room again, still full of small transmissions.

tracks.title: Rain Builds an Orchestra
tracks.creativeDirection: Ordinary sounds assembling and dissolving like a rain orchestra

segments.text: [softly] Let listening open. Imagine the room is an orchestra warming up beneath a roof of rain.
Find the lowest sound you can hear... a hum, engine, pipe, or distant vibration. Let it be the bass line.
Notice a higher sound... a bird, electronic tone, breath, or faint hiss. No need to hold it.
Listen for rhythm. Some sounds repeat; others arrive once and leave their chair empty.
Shift to the sound closest to the left... then closest to the right. Let attention move like a microphone on a slow rail.
Hear something in front... then behind... without turning the head or searching hard.
Notice silence as part of the arrangement. A rest in music is still held by the song.
Let every sound play together without choosing a favourite. The orchestra assembles itself and dissolves itself.
[reassuringly] If thought has been narrating, let that inner voice become one more instrument, then return to hearing.
[softly] Open your eyes and carry the wide listening field into the next minute.

tracks.title: The Museum of Borrowed Costumes
tracks.creativeDirection: Roles and identities displayed as useful costumes in a moonlit museum

segments.text: [softly] Settle and let breathing become ordinary. Imagine walking through a museum where every role you have worn is displayed as a costume.
Notice one role: friend, worker, child, helper, outsider, expert. See it hanging beneath a small museum light.
Quietly ask: what notices this role? Wait without replacing the question with a clever answer.
A memory appears like an old coat. It belongs to your history, yet it can also be observed from here.
A judgment appears: I am this kind of person. Place that sentence beside the costume and notice the space around both.
[thoughtfully] Roles are not false; they are useful clothing for particular rooms. The inquiry asks whether the wearer is larger than any single outfit.
Notice a sound, a sensation, and a thought. Each becomes an exhibit inside awareness. What is the open museum that contains them?
If the mind produces an answer, display that answer too. Let it stand beneath glass for a moment.
Drop the question and rest as simple noticing. Costumes remain, stories remain, and the room around them stays spacious.
[reassuringly] You do not need to lose identity. You can wear your name gently without sewing it to the sky.
[softly] Feel the body here. Leave the museum wearing whatever role the next moment needs, and open your eyes when ready.

tracks.title: The Name Tags in the Cloud Archive
tracks.creativeDirection: A cloud archive storing labels while awareness remains unfiled

segments.text: [softly] Rest comfortably and imagine a quiet archive floating above the city, storing every label the mind has collected.
Let your name appear on a small glowing tag. Notice that the name is known. What is aware of knowing it?
Add another label: successful... awkward... tired... kind... too much... not enough. Watch the archive receive it.
Ask gently: am I the label, or am I also the space in which the label is read? No final answer is needed.
Notice a thought uploading itself. Then notice the tiny gap before the next thought arrives.
Feel an emotion as data in the body: warmth, pressure, movement. What notices the signal before naming it?
[thoughtfully] The archive is useful. Memory and identity help you navigate. Yet the present awareness cannot be fully compressed into a folder.
Let all labels float at once without selecting one as the final truth. Rest in the capacity to notice them.
If confusion appears, notice confusion. If spaciousness appears, notice spaciousness. Neither receives administrator privileges.
Return to the ordinary body, with its history, needs, and name. Inquiry can make identity lighter without deleting it.
[softly] Let the archive drift into the clouds. Open your eyes and return to the useful world of names.

tracks.title: The Violet Compass
tracks.creativeDirection: A violet compass resting lightly behind the brow

segments.text: [softly] Sit comfortably and soften the muscles around the eyes. Let attention approach the space between the eyebrows without strain.
Imagine a small violet compass resting behind the brow. It does not predict the future; it simply gives attention a place to return.
Feel one inhale and exhale while the compass needle settles. Keep the gaze soft behind closed eyelids.
When thought pulls north, south, yesterday, or tomorrow, notice the journey and return to the centre point.
No colour or sensation is required. The compass can be imagined, faint, or absent while attention remains gentle.
Broaden briefly to the whole forehead, temples, and face. Release any pressure before returning to the small point.
[thoughtfully] Rest with centre and spaciousness together... one quiet needle floating inside a much wider sky.
If an image appears, let it change. If darkness remains, let darkness be complete enough.
Continue the simple cycle: wandering... noticing... returning to the violet coordinate.
[reassuringly] Clarity may come or not come. The practice is attention, not a promise of special perception.
Let the compass grow transparent. Include breath, chest, hands, and the contact points beneath you.
Hear sounds in the room while keeping a faint sense of the brow. Inner and outer coordinates can coexist.
[softly] Move your hands, open your eyes, and let the compass become an ordinary memory.

tracks.title: A Blue Window in the Snow
tracks.creativeDirection: A blue window glowing gently in a quiet snowy landscape

segments.text: [softly] Sit tall without becoming rigid. Let the face soften and place gentle attention between the eyebrows.
Imagine a small blue window glowing in a house surrounded by snow. It is simply a visual anchor, not a supernatural claim.
Notice the dark space behind the eyelids around that window. Let the image remain small and easy.
Breathe naturally. With each exhale, imagine snow settling without needing the world to become silent.
Thoughts may leave footprints across the field. See them, then return to the blue window.
If the forehead tightens, release the image and feel the whole face. Return only when the point feels comfortable.
Rest with the window for several breaths. No need to look through it or discover what is inside.
[thoughtfully] Attention can be both precise and gentle, like one lit square held by miles of soft weather.
Let wandering be another snowfall. Notice it accumulating, then gently clear a path back.
Release effort for a moment and rest in the whole inner landscape, window included.
Begin feeling the body below the face... throat... chest... belly... hands... legs.
Let the snow scene fade while sounds and temperature return to the foreground.
[softly] Open your eyes when ready. Carry the steadiness of one quiet window into the room.

tracks.title: A Comet Does Not Need Chasing
tracks.creativeDirection: An urge passing through awareness like a bright comet

segments.text: [softly] Pause somewhere safe. This is for observing an ordinary urge, not replacing help in an immediate safety or medical situation.
Name what is here: craving... pulling... wanting. Imagine it as a comet entering the edge of your sky.
Locate the urge in the body. Notice pressure, heat, tightness, movement, or restless energy.
The comet can be bright without giving instructions. Watch its tail, speed, and changing shape.
Notice any thought that says now, always, or impossible. Let the words travel behind the comet rather than steering your body.
[reassuringly] Intensity may rise. A brighter moment does not mean you must chase it or make it disappear.
Rate the urge from zero to ten, then check again after several breaths. Observe change without demanding reduction.
Feel the body beneath the sky: feet, seat, hands, breath. You are more than the streak of light passing through.
Notice whether the urge has moved, sharpened, faded, or stayed. All are useful observations.
[thoughtfully] Choice can wait until the comet is no longer filling the whole window. Remain here for a few more breaths.
[softly] Let the comet continue beyond the horizon. Return to the room and choose the next action deliberately.

tracks.title: The Train Can Leave Without You
tracks.creativeDirection: An urge arriving and departing like a neon train at a platform

segments.text: [softly] Find a safe pause. Imagine standing on a quiet platform while an ordinary urge approaches like a train in the distance.
Name the urge without boarding it. Wanting is here... impatience is here... a train is arriving.
Feel where arrival happens in the body: hands, mouth, chest, belly, legs. Notice the first vibration on the rails.
The train grows louder. Observe colour, pressure, temperature, and movement without stepping toward the door.
Thoughts may advertise the destination. Hear the announcement and remain on the platform.
[reassuringly] You do not need to fight the train. Let it be present at full size while breathing remains natural.
Notice the crest: perhaps urgency peaks, flickers, or changes location. Keep both feet connected to the ground.
Listen for the first sign of departure. It may be subtle: one loosened muscle, one quieter sentence, one second of space.
The train may linger or another may follow. Urges can repeat without becoming permanent orders.
[thoughtfully] Let your next choice come from the person on the platform, not from the loudspeaker.
[softly] Watch the red lights travel away. Feel the room around you and decide the next step in your own time.

tracks.title: The Museum of Unfinished Things
tracks.creativeDirection: An after-hours museum where unfinished experiences are allowed to remain

segments.text: [softly] Settle and imagine entering a museum after closing, where unfinished feelings and unanswered questions are allowed to remain on display.
Notice what is present now. Perhaps tension, sadness, restlessness, numbness, or something without a name.
Imagine placing the experience on a simple pedestal. Acceptance does not call it beautiful or permanent. It only stops hiding it in the basement.
Feel where the exhibit appears in the body. Notice shape, pressure, temperature, and movement.
The mind may arrive with tools and warning signs. Let the repair crew sit on a bench for a little while.
Quietly say: this is part of the room right now. It does not have to become the entire museum.
[reassuringly] If resistance appears, give it a small display card too. The wish not to feel this is also something being felt.
Broaden attention to sounds, breath, hands, feet, and the surface beneath you. More than one exhibit can exist at once.
For several breaths, allow the unfinished thing to remain without completing its story.
[thoughtfully] Acceptance is not permission for harm and not a contract with forever. It is honest admission to the room you are already in.
Imagine the gallery lights softening. The exhibit can stay while you walk toward the exit.
[softly] Move gently and open your eyes. Leave the museum without needing to take every unfinished thing home.

tracks.title: A River for the Fallen Leaves
tracks.creativeDirection: A slow river making room for every leaf without holding it

segments.text: [softly] Let the body rest and imagine sitting beside a slow river beneath autumn trees.
Notice the experience you are resisting. Name it gently if a name comes: fear... pressure... grief... wanting... no.
Feel where it lives in the body. Let sensation be a fallen leaf touching water for the first time.
Acceptance is the river making room for the leaf. It does not approve the storm that brought it down.
Notice the urge to push, solve, explain, or cling. Let that urge become another leaf beside the first.
Quietly repeat: this is what is here now... and this moment is allowed to be known.
Observe whether sensation moves, stays, widens, or changes temperature. No movement is required.
[reassuringly] The river is wider than one leaf. Include sounds, breath, contact points, and the room around the difficulty.
If a thought returns, let it touch the surface and travel at its own pace.
[thoughtfully] You can accept the reality of this moment and still choose boundaries, repair, or change in the next one.
Let the river continue without watching every bend. Feel the body beside it, breathing and supported.
[softly] Open your eyes when ready. Carry the river's spaciousness, not the leaves.

tracks.title: The Ember in the Snow
tracks.creativeDirection: A warm ember resting within a silent field of snow

segments.text: [softly] Place the flame near eye level and sit comfortably. Blink whenever needed, and stop for pain, dizziness, excessive tearing, or lasting eye discomfort.
Let the flame become one warm ember resting in a wide field of snow. Keep the gaze gentle rather than rigid.
Notice the blue near the wick, the gold above it, and the soft halo around the edges.
Blink naturally. Each time the eyes reopen, meet the ember without trying to pin it in place.
Allow attention to rest on the quiet contrast between warmth and darkness.
Close your eyes. Notice any after-image floating behind the eyelids like an ember beneath snow.
Let the image change colour, move, fade, or disappear. There is nothing to preserve.
If no image appears, rest with the dark field itself and feel the body breathing.
Allow the eye muscles to soften completely.
[softly] Open the eyes and return to the flame. Notice movement without losing the centre.
The ember leans and rises, never holding one shape for long.
Stay with colour and light while allowing easy blinks.
Let the wide dark room support the small bright point.
Close your eyes again. Watch the remembered ember or the simple darkness where it had been.
Feel forehead, cheeks, jaw, and eyes becoming quiet as snow.
Widen to the whole body and the sounds around you.
[softly] Open your eyes slowly. Leave the ember in the flame and carry only the steadiness.

tracks.title: A Candle Beyond the Spaceship Glass
tracks.creativeDirection: A candle appearing like a tiny sun beyond a spaceship window

segments.text: [softly] Sit with the flame near eye level. Keep blinking naturally and stop if the eyes become painful, dizzy, excessively watery, or persistently uncomfortable.
Imagine the flame as a tiny sun beyond the glass of a quiet spacecraft.
Rest the gaze near the wick. Let the surrounding room become deep space without forcing it away.
Notice flicker, colour, brightness, and the small dark centre. Gentle attention is enough.
Blink and return, as though the navigation window refreshes itself.
Close your eyes. Notice whether the tiny sun remains as an after-image behind the lids.
Watch it drift, pulse, reverse colour, or fade through the inner dark.
No image is also a complete experience. Rest with the window closed.
Feel breath and body while the eyes recover.
[softly] Open the eyes and find the flame again, one bright coordinate in a wide cabin.
Let attention stay near the centre without hardening the brow.
Notice that the flame changes constantly while remaining easy to recognise.
Rest with this small sun for several natural breaths.
Close the eyes once more and allow the outer flame to become inner memory.
Let the image travel beyond the window and disappear into a larger darkness.
Feel the whole face, whole body, and ordinary room returning.
[softly] Open your eyes slowly. Navigation is complete; take your time moving on.

tracks.title: The Moonlit Accordion
tracks.creativeDirection: The lower ribs opening like a quiet moonlit accordion

segments.text: [softly] Sit or lie comfortably. Place a hand on the belly if useful and let several breaths happen without changing them.
Notice movement beneath the hand. Invite the belly and lower ribs to make a little more room on the next inhale.
Imagine a moonlit accordion beneath the ribs opening easily... then folding home on the exhale.
Keep the breath quiet. The chest may move too; nothing needs to be locked.
Try an easy rhythm: inhale one... two... three... exhale one... two... three... only while comfortable.
[reassuringly] Release counting at the first sign of strain. Ordinary breathing is always available.
Feel the lower ribs widen to the sides and perhaps slightly into the back.
Let the accordion play almost silently for several breaths, with no need for maximum depth.
If dizziness, tingling, or discomfort appears, stop shaping the breath and rest.
Notice how exhaling can finish without squeezing. Let the folds close by themselves.
Remove the hand if you wish and see whether the body remembers the easy movement.
[softly] Release the exercise. Return to natural breathing and the sounds of the room.

tracks.title: The Cave That Breathes with the Tide
tracks.creativeDirection: A tidal cave expanding and settling with comfortable breath

segments.text: [softly] Find an easy position and let the breath arrive as it is. One hand may rest on the belly and one on the chest.
On an inhale, invite gentle movement beneath the lower hand. On the exhale, let the belly settle without pushing.
Imagine the lower ribs as a cave beside the sea. Water enters quietly and the walls make a little space.
The tide leaves in its own time. Keep every breath smaller than strain.
Notice expansion toward the front, sides, and back... a three-dimensional room rather than a balloon forced outward.
Let several breaths follow their own tide with no counting.
[reassuringly] If you feel dizzy, tingly, or uncomfortable, return to ordinary breathing immediately.
Try a soft count only if it helps: in one... two... three... out one... two... three.
Release the count and listen for the quiet point between waves, without holding the breath there.
Allow shoulders, throat, and jaw to remain unhelpfully relaxed while the diaphragm does less dramatic work.
Let the hands grow light and trust the body to continue breathing.
[softly] Leave the cave beside the tide. Feel the room and breathe however feels natural now.

tracks.title: The Moth Finds the Porch Light
tracks.creativeDirection: Attention returning like a moth to one warm porch light

segments.text: [softly] Choose one comfortable breath sensation as your porch light: nostrils, chest, or belly.
Feel one inhale and one exhale. Let attention rest near the small warm signal.
Imagine the mind as a moth circling through the dark. Wandering is what minds do.
When you notice thought, sound, or feeling has carried attention away, name it lightly and return to the porch light.
[reassuringly] The return is the practice. No flight path needs to be erased.
Stay with three breaths: one... two... three... feeling each from beginning to end.
Release counting and notice the most vivid detail of breathing.
If restlessness appears, feel it for one moment, then return without argument.
Again and again, the moth discovers the light. Each discovery is new.
Rest with fewer words now: breathing... wandering... noticing... home.
Widen attention to include the whole body and room.
[softly] Open your eyes. Let attention fly freely, remembering that it knows a way back.

tracks.title: One Clear Frequency
tracks.creativeDirection: Tuning attention back to one clear frequency in a sky of static

segments.text: [softly] Settle and choose the breath as one clear frequency. Feel it where the signal is easiest to detect.
Listen with the body to one full inhale... one full exhale.
Thoughts may produce static, music, headlines, and weather reports. Notice the broadcast.
Turn the dial gently back to breathing. No need to smash the radio.
When sound distracts you, name hearing. When thought distracts you, name thinking. Then tune back.
[reassuringly] Every noticed distraction proves awareness is working.
Count five breaths if useful. One... two... three... four... five... then release the numbers.
Stay near the smallest breath detail you can feel without straining.
Let static rise and fall around the signal. You do not need perfect reception.
Rest in the repeated movement of losing and finding the frequency.
Expand hearing to every channel in the room while keeping a faint sense of breath.
[softly] Open your eyes and carry one clear frequency into the next task.

tracks.title: The Campsite Check-In
tracks.creativeDirection: Checking sensory coordinates around a safe midnight campsite

segments.text: [softly] Keep your eyes open or softly lowered. Imagine checking the coordinates of a calm campsite after dark.
Find five things you can see. Colour, edge, shadow, texture, light. Let each become a marker around the tent.
One... two... three... four... five... You are here, in this particular place.
Notice four things you can feel: feet, clothing, seat, air, hands, or warmth.
Let contact points become tent pegs holding attention close to the ground.
Find three sounds. Perhaps one is distant, one is near, and one belongs to your body.
Notice two scents or two qualities of the air. Faint and neutral both count.
Notice one taste. Let the smallest ordinary sensation complete the campsite map.
[reassuringly] Thoughts can remain beyond the firelight. They are not the only coordinates available.
Rest with the strongest physical contact point for several breaths.
Look around and name where you are, the approximate time, and one gentle next action.
[softly] Pack only what you need. Leave the campsite slowly and return to the ordinary room.

tracks.title: A Small Kitchen at Dawn
tracks.creativeDirection: Five senses returning in a familiar kitchen at first light

segments.text: [softly] Let the eyes stay open. Imagine attention arriving in a small kitchen just before sunrise.
Notice five visible details as though morning light has found them for the first time.
Shape... colour... pattern... reflection... shadow. Let seeing return you to this room.
Find four touch sensations: fabric, floor, chair, temperature, weight, or the meeting of hands.
Notice three sounds, including the quiet mechanical sounds a home makes by itself.
Find two scents or air qualities. Perhaps clean, warm, cool, dry, familiar, or almost absent.
Notice one taste. Neutral is still a taste and ordinary is still present.
[thoughtfully] Let all five senses share one countertop of awareness. Nothing needs to dominate.
Feel both feet or the back of the body as one dependable surface.
Name the day, the place, and one thing you can do next without rushing.
Look around again and notice one detail that feels pleasant or simply okay.
[softly] Let morning continue. Move into the next moment with the room still around you.

tracks.title: The Greenhouse of Sleeping Flowers
tracks.creativeDirection: A moonlit greenhouse closing flower by flower through a detailed body rotation

segments.text: [softly] Lie down and make every practical adjustment now. Let the body be warm and supported. Yoga Nidra invites deep rest; you may remain awake or drift near sleep.
Imagine lying inside a moonlit greenhouse where thousands of flowers are closing for the night. Feel the whole body resting as one quiet garden.
Bring attention to the right thumb... index finger... middle finger... ring finger... little finger... palm... back of the hand... wrist.
Right forearm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... right side of the ribs... waist... hip.
Right thigh... knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of the foot... big toe... second... third... fourth... little toe.
Now left thumb... index finger... middle finger... ring finger... little finger... palm... back of the hand... wrist.
Left forearm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... left ribs... waist... hip.
Left thigh... knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of the foot... big toe... second... third... fourth... little toe.
Feel both heels... backs of the legs... backs of the thighs... buttocks... lower back... middle back... upper back... both shoulder blades.
Notice the belly... navel... lower ribs... centre of the chest... collarbones... throat. Each flower folds inward without being forced.
Bring attention to the jaw... lower lip... upper lip... corners of the mouth... gums... teeth... the whole tongue resting wide and heavy.
Feel the inside of the cheeks... outer cheeks... nose... nostrils... bridge of the nose... space beneath the eyes.
Right eyelid... left eyelid... muscles around both eyes... right eyebrow... left eyebrow... space between the eyebrows.
Forehead... right temple... left temple... ears... back of the head... crown... entire scalp. Let every tiny facial muscle stop holding the day.
Feel the whole right side of the body... whole left side... back body... front body... the entire body at once.
[reassuringly] Nothing has to become numb or heavy. Sensation may remain bright. Rest is the permission to stop managing it.
Imagine moonlight moving slowly across the greenhouse roof while breathing continues beneath every closed flower.
Rest with the whole body as one field of quiet sensation, complete from scalp to toes.
Begin remembering the room around the greenhouse... its sounds... temperature... and the surface carrying you.
[softly] Deepen the breath, move fingers and toes, and stretch gently if wanted. Open your eyes as the greenhouse receives first light.

tracks.title: The Starship Sleep Deck
tracks.creativeDirection: A starship sleep deck powering down every body system in detailed sequence

segments.text: [softly] Lie down, support the body, and settle the temperature around you. Imagine entering the sleep deck of a starship travelling on automatic.
Feel the complete outline of the body. The ship is moving, but you have no controls to operate for a while.
Right thumb... index... middle... ring... little finger... palm... back of hand... wrist. Each panel turns from blue to dark.
Right forearm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... ribs... waist... hip.
Right thigh... kneecap... back of knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of foot... each of the five toes.
Left thumb... index... middle... ring... little finger... palm... back of hand... wrist.
Left forearm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... ribs... waist... hip.
Left thigh... kneecap... back of knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of foot... each of the five toes.
Both heels... calves... backs of knees... backs of thighs... pelvis... lower back... middle back... upper back... shoulder blades.
Lower belly... navel... upper belly... lower ribs... chest... collarbones... throat. The central deck grows quiet.
Jaw hinge... chin... lower lip... upper lip... corners of mouth... teeth... gums... tongue... root of the tongue. Let the mouth rest completely.
Cheeks... nose... nostrils... bridge... space around the eyes... eyelids... tiny muscles beneath the eyes.
Right eyebrow... left eyebrow... space between them... forehead... temples... ears... back of head... crown... whole scalp.
Feel the entire face powered down without disappearing. Breathing and swallowing can continue by themselves.
Whole right side... whole left side... both together... whole back... whole front... complete body inside the sleep deck.
[thoughtfully] A thought may cross the monitoring screen. Let automatic systems handle it without waking the crew.
Rest as one field of sensation suspended among distant stars.
Sense the breath entering and leaving the complete body, with no part needing to assist.
Remember the real room around you and the ordinary planet supporting everything.
[softly] Bring movement to fingers, toes, face, and limbs. Open your eyes when ready; the ship has carried you home.

tracks.title: The Cabin Under Quiet Snow
tracks.creativeDirection: A warm cabin becoming still beneath deep snow through an intricate body scan

segments.text: [softly] Lie down and arrange the body for twenty minutes of unhurried rest. Imagine a warm cabin while snow gathers quietly outside.
Feel the whole body beneath its coverings. Nothing needs to be held up. The roof, walls, and earth are doing the work.
Right thumb... first finger... second... third... fourth... palm... back of hand... wrist. Snow softens every edge.
Right lower arm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... right ribs... waist... hip.
Right thigh... knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of foot... big toe through little toe.
Left thumb... first finger... second... third... fourth... palm... back of hand... wrist.
Left lower arm... elbow... upper arm... shoulder... armpit... left ribs... waist... hip.
Left thigh... knee... shin... calf... ankle... heel... sole... top of foot... big toe through little toe.
Backs of both legs... buttocks... tailbone... lower back... middle back... upper back... shoulder blades... back of neck.
Lower belly... navel... upper belly... ribs... heart area... collarbones... throat. The cabin stove glows without needing attention.
Chin... jaw muscles... lower lip... upper lip... corners of mouth... teeth... gums... tongue lying loose in the floor of the mouth.
Inner cheeks... outer cheeks... nose... nostrils... bridge of nose... skin beneath the eyes.
Right eye... left eye... both eyelids... muscles around the eyes... eyebrows... the soft space between them.
Forehead smoothing... temples... ears... back of skull... top of head... entire scalp. Let the face finish its last conversation.
Feel the entire right side... entire left side... both sides together... back body... front body... complete body.
[reassuringly] You may feel heavy, light, restless, or nearly asleep. The snow does not require a particular kind of quiet.
Rest as the whole cabin, not one room at a time. Breath moves softly through the warm interior.
Let several long moments pass with the complete body known at once.
Begin hearing the real room. Feel temperature, coverings, floor, and the shape of the body returning.
[softly] Move fingers and toes, roll the head gently, and stretch if desired. Open your eyes as snowlight reaches the windows.
